slides.title: City tax|why you pay it at the desk
slides.body: A local tax, not a hotel extra.

slides.title: What it is.
slides.body: A local tax charged per person, per night, in many cities and regions.

slides.title: Who sets it.
slides.body: The city or region, not the hotel. The amount varies from place to place.

slides.title: Often paid on site.
slides.body: Many hotels collect it at check-in or checkout, separately from your room rate.

slides.title: It can depend on stars.
slides.body: In some cities a higher-rated hotel means a higher tax per night.

slides.title: Kids may be exempt.
slides.body: Some places exempt children under a set age. Rules differ by city.

slides.title: Read the booking details.
slides.body: Look for "payable at the property" so it's never a surprise.

slides.title: No surprises at checkout.
slides.body: Compare hotels and read every detail on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
You booked the room, then the hotel asks for a few more euros at the desk. That's usually the city tax.

Many cities and regions charge a small local tax per person, per night. The city sets it, not the hotel, and it's often collected on site at check-in or checkout. In some places it depends on the hotel's star rating, and children can be exempt. Look for "payable at the property" in your booking details.

slides.title: Beach hotel?|6 things to check first
slides.body: Read these before you pick the room.

slides.title: How close is the sea.
slides.body: "Near the beach" can mean steps away or a road to cross. Check the map.

slides.title: Private or public beach.
slides.body: Some hotels have their own stretch of sand, others share the public beach.

slides.title: Sunbeds and umbrellas.
slides.body: Included, limited or paid on the beach? It's often in the hotel details.

slides.title: Sea view or side view.
slides.body: "Side sea view" is a different room. Read the room name carefully.

slides.title: Sand or pebbles.
slides.body: Many Mediterranean beaches are pebbly. Pack water shoes if needed.

slides.title: Open all year?
slides.body: Some beach hotels close or slow down in winter. Check your dates.

slides.title: Sea first, then the room.
slides.body: Compare beach hotels on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
A beach hotel can mean a lot of different things once you arrive.

Check how close the sea really is, whether the beach is private or public, how sunbeds work, if your room is sea view or side sea view, whether the beach is sand or pebbles, and that the hotel is open on your dates.

Save this for next summer.

slides.title: Capri|where to stay, by vibe
slides.body: 5 areas, 5 different trips.

slides.title: Capri town
slides.body: Around the Piazzetta, with cafes, boutiques and evening strolls. Busy with day-trippers by day.

slides.title: Anacapri
slides.body: Higher up on the west side, calmer in the evening, with the chairlift to Monte Solaro.

slides.title: Marina Grande
slides.body: The main port where ferries arrive, with the funicular up to Capri town.

slides.title: Marina Piccola
slides.body: On the south coast, with small beaches, bathing spots and views of the Faraglioni.

slides.title: Tragara
slides.body: A quiet area near Capri town, on the walk to the Faraglioni viewpoint.

slides.title: Which one is yours?
slides.body: Compare Capri hotels on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
Capri is small, but where you sleep changes the whole trip.

Want to be in the middle of it? Capri town, around the Piazzetta. Calmer evenings? Anacapri. Easy arrival by ferry? Marina Grande. Swimming first? Marina Piccola. Quiet nights and views of the Faraglioni? Tragara.

slides.title: Staying a week?|Try an aparthotel
slides.body: Hotel services, apartment space.

slides.title: What it is.
slides.body: An apartment with a kitchenette, run like a hotel with a reception and cleaning.

slides.title: Eat in when you want.
slides.body: Breakfast at home, dinner out. Handy on longer stays.

slides.title: More room to spread out.
slides.body: A separate living area often helps with families or long trips.

slides.title: Look for a washing machine.
slides.body: Laundry on site means you can pack lighter.

slides.title: Check the cleaning.
slides.body: Housekeeping can be less frequent than in a hotel. It's in the details.

slides.title: Check reception hours.
slides.body: Some have a desk part of the day only, or self check-in. Plan your arrival.

slides.title: Long trip coming up?
slides.body: Find aparthotels and hotels on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
For a week or more, an aparthotel can be easier than a classic room.

You get a kitchenette and more space, with hotel services like a reception and cleaning. Look for a washing machine so you can pack lighter, and check how often housekeeping comes and when the reception is open before you arrive.

Save this for your next long trip.
